title: cmdpal dock new auto-hide bug with bottom position
summary: Command Palette dock auto-hide repeatedly hides and reveals when docked at the bottom and the pointer reaches the Windows taskbar. A second user supplied a public recording confirming the behavior.

judgment.rationale: The report provides a short deterministic sequence and a second user supplied a recording of the same bottom-dock/taskbar interaction. The remaining work is maintainer-side reproduction against the current build to isolate the trigger boundary.
evidence: Set Command Palette dock position to bottom.
Move the pointer into the Windows taskbar.
The dock repeatedly hides and reveals instead of remaining shown.
A second user confirmed the issue and attached a public recording.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on the current Command Palette build while tracing the bottom-edge auto-hide trigger and taskbar overlap.

fix_assessment.rationale: The symptom is consistent with competing taskbar-edge enter/leave or visibility triggers in the bottom-docked auto-hide state; focused reproduction is needed before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Debounce bottom-edge auto-hide transitions across the taskbar boundary
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Likely competing pointer-boundary and dock visibility transitions repeatedly reinterpret movement into the bottom taskbar as both show and hide input.
plan: Trace the bottom-docked auto-hide pointer and visibility state transitions.
Treat the taskbar-adjacent activation strip as part of one stable hover state instead of alternating enter/leave signals.
Add coverage for bottom docking with Windows taskbar auto-hide both enabled and disabled.
verification: Reproduce the issue with bottom docking and confirm moving into the taskbar reveals the dock once without oscillation.

confidence.rationale: The deterministic taskbar-boundary symptom strongly suggests a state-transition conflict, but tracing is needed to identify the exact handler.

issue_context.summary: Bottom-docked Command Palette auto-hide oscillates when the cursor moves into the Windows taskbar.
known_information: The issue occurs with Command Palette docked at the bottom and auto-hide enabled.
Moving the pointer into the taskbar triggers the failure.
A second user reproduced it and attached a recording.
inferences: The bottom taskbar boundary may generate conflicting activation and dismissal transitions for the dock.
issue_context.analysis: The public sequence and recording are sufficient for maintainer reproduction. The correct next step is tracing the dock auto-hide state machine, not asking the reporter for generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the original report and the second-user confirmation recording reference.

actions.label: Approve bottom-dock auto-hide stabilization design

design.title: Approve bottom-dock auto-hide stabilization design
design.prompt: Design a focused fix for PowerToys issue 50515. Trace Command Palette bottom-dock auto-hide pointer and visibility transitions at the Windows taskbar boundary, eliminate competing show/hide state changes without weakening activation behavior, and add coverage for taskbar auto-hide enabled and disabled.

reproduce.version: Current main or a build at least as new as 0.101.2492
prerequisites: Windows taskbar visible at the bottom edge
steps: Set Command Palette dock position to Bottom.
Move the pointer from the desktop into the Windows taskbar area.
Observe dock visibility transitions while moving along and away from the taskbar boundary.
reproduce.expected: The dock reveals once and remains stable while the pointer is in its activation/taskbar boundary; it must not repeatedly hide and reveal.
